On your Mac, open System Settings → Network → your phone → Details → Proxies. Turn on Web proxy, Secure web proxy and SOCKS proxy, each with this address and port %1$d.

This phone doesn\'t tell apps which Wi‑Fi is its hotspot, so hotspot sharing can\'t start. Sharing over USB still works.
Proxy for devices on the hotspot

On your iPhone, open Settings → Wi‑Fi and tap the info button (ⓘ) next to this phone\'s hotspot. Tap Configure Proxy → Manual, enter this server and port %1$d, leave Authentication off, then tap Save.
It only changes this hotspot on the iPhone, so you can leave it on to use the VPN whenever you\'re on this hotspot. To use the hotspot without the VPN, set Configure Proxy back to Off and tap Save.
Not sharing now. If your Mac still has the proxies on, its browsing won\'t work: paste this into Terminal on the Mac to turn them off.

Not sharing now, so a device that still has the proxy on can\'t browse. Turn sharing back on, or turn its proxy off: on an iPhone, set the hotspot\'s Configure Proxy to Off and tap Save; on a Mac, paste this into Terminal.
Enter the server and port below on the device. Everything that follows the proxy goes through the VPN, including your tailnet and home network, which it can\'t reach that way.

The device loads its rules from this phone. Your tailnet, home network and names like truenas go direct; everything else goes through the VPN. Once the device has the rules, it should go direct while the VPN reconnects or is off.
Set every device the same way: this choice also decides what this phone does while the VPN reconnects.

Direct: Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10, .ts.net), .local and plain names, this connection\'s own network, and home %1$s. Names are matched as written, so a custom domain goes through the VPN even if it points home.
Direct: Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10, .ts.net), .local and plain names, and this connection\'s own network. Names are matched as written, so a custom domain goes through the VPN even if it points home.
Addresses here go direct, so the device reaches them through Tailscale instead of the VPN.
For example 192.168.68.0/22. Separate several with commas.
Use ranges like 192.168.68.0/22, up to 16, separated by commas.
Or paste the command into Terminal on your Mac. It finds the phone\'s connection and sets Automatic proxy configuration there, asking for your Mac password. Run it again if this address changes.
On your iPhone, open Settings → Wi‑Fi and tap the info button (ⓘ) next to this phone\'s hotspot. Tap Configure Proxy → Automatic, enter this URL, then tap Save.

It only changes this hotspot on the iPhone. If the iPhone joins the hotspot while this phone isn\'t sharing (sharing off, the VPN not connected, or the app closed), it may not be able to load the rules or browse. If that happens, set Configure Proxy back to Off.
On your Mac, open System Settings → Network → your phone → Details → Proxies. Turn on Automatic proxy configuration with this URL, and turn the other proxies off.

A Mac on the hotspot can paste the Terminal command instead. A Mac keeps it for Wi‑Fi everywhere, so run the turn-off command before you leave the hotspot.

Only apps that use the system proxy go through the VPN, such as Safari and Chrome. Other traffic, and calls or games that use UDP, still go around it. A device with the proxy on can only browse while sharing is on here.
